targets.title: Physical exercise as interoceptive exposure within a brief cognitive-behavioral treatment for anxiety-sensitive women.
targets.evidence_quote:
The aim of the current study was to further
explore the role of running as the IE component
of a brief CBT for high AS women, by
replicating and extending results from a

targets.outcome_quote:
As a result of repeated exposure to
the running IE component of the intervention,
high AS participants, but not low AS participants, experienced a decrease in catastrophic
cognitions about the sensations associated
with running and a decrease in fear of these
arousal sensations. This result is consistent
with results from our previous process study
(Sabourin et al., 2008). As expected, high AS
participants also experienced decreases in
somatic reactions to running over time.
Contrary to predictions, however, the low AS
group did not reveal a decline in somatic
reactions to the running.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Cognitive and affective changes are explicitly consistent with the original process study. The original had somatic reductions in both groups; the present discussion states that the low-AS group did not decline, contrary to predictions. No overall verdict about the entire replication overrides these comparisons. Watt et al. concerns the larger outcome study; its findings are not independently tested by this process report.

reasoning: Title, four authors and article pages verified in complete author-hosted article, including references. New participants retest the published process-study findings; the separately reported larger outcome study is not a second target.
